h1:
What to Eat in Phayao
12 Dishes Worth Trying
intro: Phayao is a small town that eats far better than its size. It has the classic northern dishes — khanom jeen nam ngiao and gaeng hang lay — alongside fish pulled straight from Kwan Phayao lake and cooked right by the water, plus a row of lakeside cafes where the sunset is good enough that people happily drive in just to sit for hours. This is what locals in Phayao actually eat, and what visitors shouldn't skip.

blocks.html: Most people coming to Phayao for the first time come for the lake and the temples, but it's usually the food that pulls them back. The town packs three kinds of eating close together: old-school northern restaurants in town, fresh freshwater fish from Kwan Phayao, and a new wave of cafes along the water. We've picked 12 things worth trying, with the real shop names and the areas you can head straight to.

The food that really stands for Phayao is northern Thai, above all khanom jeen nam ngiao — and Phayao has plenty of versions of it. Each shop has its own recipe; some use the Nan style, some the Chiang Rai style, and the flavour tends to be bolder here than elsewhere.

items.name: Khanom Jeen Nam Ngiao (Khanom Sen Nam Ngiao)
items.blurb: Phayao's classic breakfast: an orange broth coloured by red kapok flowers and tomato, with pork blood cubes and minced pork, ladled over rice noodles and eaten with fresh veg, crispy pork rind, and roasted bird's-eye chili. Up north, rice noodles are called 'khanom sen', which is why you'll also see it written as khanom sen nam ngiao.

items.name: Khao Soi (chicken/beef)
items.blurb: Egg noodles in a coconut-curry broth made with northern curry paste, topped with crispy fried noodles and eaten with pickled greens, shallots, and lime. Phayao has several old-school khao soi shops in town, some of them going for more than 40 years.

items.name: Gaeng Hang Lay
items.blurb: A northern pork-belly curry, sour-sweet-salty and well-rounded, made with ginger and hang lay spice mix and simmered until the pork falls apart. It's just right with sticky rice, and you'll find it at northern restaurants and the lakeside spots.

items.name: Kuaytiao Nam Ngiao
items.blurb: The rice-noodle version of nam ngiao, for anyone who prefers a chewier noodle than the soft khanom jeen strands. Plenty of shops in Phayao serve both side by side, so you can take your pick.

items.name: Sai Ua + Crispy Pork Rind
items.blurb: Fragrant grilled herb sausage, good as a snack or with sticky rice, paired with crunchy pork rind. It's both a nibble and a take-home gift, easy to find at the morning market and souvenir shops around town.

items.name: Kuaytiao Kha Mu
items.blurb: Phayao's stewed pork-leg noodle shops don't hold back — tender, fall-apart pork leg with all the trimmings. It's the heavy, satisfying bowl locals reach for when they're hungry, and the prices are friendly.

blocks.title: Tip
blocks.html: The old-school khanom jeen nam ngiao and khao soi shops are usually morning places — they open around 7–8am and sell out before the afternoon. If you want the famous ones, going mid-morning before noon is the safer bet.

blocks.text: Kwan Phayao fish — fresh freshwater fish by the water

blocks.html: Kwan Phayao is the freshwater lake that feeds the whole town. Tilapia, sheatfish, and tiny freshwater shrimp are caught fresh and cooked right by the water. What makes the spots along here special is fresh fish with a wide-open lake view, especially in the late afternoon once the sun softens.

items.name: Fried Tilapia with Fish Sauce / Lui Suan
items.blurb: A big tilapia from the lake, fried until the skin is crisp, then topped with sweet fish sauce or a punchy lui-suan herb salad. Almost every lakeside spot has it, and it's the single most-ordered plate.

items.name: Fried Sheatfish with Garlic
items.blurb: Sheatfish is a soft-fleshed freshwater fish from Kwan Phayao, fried with garlic until fragrant and meltingly tender. It's a dish that places like Krua Aurora are known for.

items.name: Fried Freshwater Shrimp
items.blurb: Tiny freshwater shrimp from the lake, battered and fried whole until crisp — easy snacking dipped in seafood sauce. It's a table staple at nearly every lakeside spot.

items.name: Miang Pla Nin Phao
items.blurb: Salt-grilled tilapia, the flesh flaked off and wrapped with fresh veg, ginger, chili, and peanuts, then drizzled with miang sauce — bright, fresh bites that make a good opener before a heavier meal.

blocks.text: Lakeside restaurants locals take you to

blocks.html: If you want to settle in for a long meal with a lake view, these are the places locals think of when they have guests in town. Most sit on the lake along the town side, an easy drive or walk from the lakeshore road. Evenings get busy, so if you're coming as a group it's worth calling ahead to book a table by the water.

items.name: Krua Aurora
items.blurb: A lakeside restaurant focused on Thai food and lake fish, using its own pesticide-free vegetables, with a strong sunset view. The dishes to order are the fried sheatfish with garlic and the miang pla nin phao.

items.name: Chitlom Chom Kwan
items.blurb: A well-known lakeside spot with a mixed menu of northern, Thai, and Isan food. Reviewers like the giant snakehead tom yum, duck laab, and gaeng hang lay, in a relaxed setting.

items.name: Niyom Suk
items.blurb: A popular restaurant with both an air-conditioned room and an outdoor lakeside section. The regular orders are the creamy tom yum, stir-fried soft-shell crab in curry powder, and fried tilapia lui suan.

items.name: So Good Phayao
items.blurb: A lakeside spot with a nice atmosphere and live music some nights. Recommended dishes are fried tilapia with fish sauce, fried freshwater shrimp, and steamed seafood curry — good for a long dinner.

blocks.title: Booking a lakeside table
blocks.html: Tables right on the water are limited and fill up fast on weekend evenings. If you're set on watching the sunset, call ahead to reserve or arrive before 5pm.

Over the last few years Phayao has seen a wave of new lakeside cafes open — some minimal and photogenic, some made for settling in to work for hours. What they share is the wide lake view and a cool breeze, making them a good afternoon stop before the evening leg of your trip.

items.name: A Ga Li Go Ingkwan
items.blurb: A white loft-style house on the lake along Phahonyothin Road, with both an air-conditioned room and a breezy balcony looking over the water. Parking is easy out front — a good place to chill in the afternoon.

items.name: The Moon 1971
items.blurb: A clean, white-toned cafe out by Mae Ka, near the University of Phayao. It's roomy, with both indoor and outdoor seating — a solid spot to settle in and work.

items.name: Yuhoo Wan Yen, Phayao Branch
items.blurb: A shaved-ice dessert shop that's a hit on social media — a good afternoon cool-down, and a nice way to finish a meal before a walk along the lake.

items: Phayao Morning Market — northern eats, sai ua, crispy pork rind, chili dips, and local vegetables all in one place, good for grabbing breakfast and souvenirs
Nam ngiao to take home — many shops bag up their nam ngiao broth to go, a popular take-home gift among northerners

faq.q: What food should I try in Phayao?
faq.a: First is khanom jeen nam ngiao (khanom sen nam ngiao), the town's classic breakfast, followed by old-school khao soi, gaeng hang lay, and fish from Kwan Phayao like fried tilapia and fried sheatfish with garlic. Finish at a lakeside cafe with a good sunset view.

faq.q: What is Kwan Phayao fish, and where's a good place to eat it?
faq.a: The favourite fish from Kwan Phayao are tilapia, sheatfish, and tiny freshwater shrimp. Lakeside spots on the town side — Krua Aurora, Chitlom Chom Kwan, Niyom Suk, and So Good Phayao — serve fresh fish with a lake view, ideal for dinner.

faq.q: How is Phayao's khanom jeen nam ngiao different from elsewhere?
faq.a: Phayao has several nam ngiao recipes — some shops use the Nan style, some the Chiang Rai style — and the broth is richer and bolder than in many places. A few shops even do a beef nam ngiao that's not easy to find in other provinces. Prices start at around ฿35–50 a bowl.

faq.q: Which Phayao lakeside cafe has the best view?
faq.a: A Ga Li Go Ingkwan is a white loft house on the lake along Phahonyothin Road, with a balcony overlooking the water, while The Moon 1971 out by Mae Ka, near the University of Phayao, is good for settling in to work. The lakeside is breezy in the late afternoon and the sunset is lovely.

faq.q: What time do Phayao's breakfast shops open?
faq.a: The khanom jeen nam ngiao and old-school khao soi shops usually open around 7–8am and sell out before the afternoon. Go mid-morning, before noon, to catch the famous spots in time.
